reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete real inner-product space in which closed bounded balls are compact, and let S be any state type. For every nonnegative real β, center u∈E, positive reals R and ε with ε≤βR², every function φ:ℝ→ℕ, every fixed deterministic pair next:S→E⊕E and update:S→E→(ℝ×E)→S, and every initial state s₀∈S, set δ=ε/R² and N=⌈φ(2β/δ) log(δR²/(ε/2))⌉₊. Here the ceiling is the natural-number ceiling, and log is the real natural logarithm.
Assume the following uniform success guarantee for this same next, update, s₀, φ and N: for every everywhere Fréchet-differentiable g:E→ℝ that is globally δ-strongly convex and whose actual gradient is globally Lipschitz with constant 2β, and for every global minimizer w of g satisfying ‖w−u‖≤R, there exist a terminal state t∈S, an output x∈E and a query count c∈ℕ such that execute next update (y↦(g(y),∇g(y))) N s₀=((t,some x),c) and g(x)−g(w)≤ε/2. The strong convexity convention subtracts (δ/2)θ(1−θ)‖x−y‖² from the convex chord bound.
Define corrected(s,y,a)=update(s,y,(a₁+(δ/2)‖y−u‖²,a₂+δ(y−u))). Then, for every everywhere Fréchet-differentiable globally convex f:E→ℝ with globally β-Lipschitz actual gradient, and every global minimizer z of f with ‖z−u‖≤R, there exist t∈S, x∈E and c∈ℕ such that execute next corrected (y↦(f(y),∇f(y))) N s₀=((t,some x),c), f(x)−f(z)≤ε, c≤⌈φ(2βR²/ε) log 2⌉₊, and c≤φ(2βR²/ε).
The execution inspects next at each state, returning a successful some x immediately on its left branch even when remaining query fuel is zero. Its right branch requests an oracle answer and increments c by one only when fuel is positive; a right branch at zero fuel instead returns none. Thus the conclusion asserts actual successful termination within the stated query budget, not merely exhaustion of that budget. The terminal state t, returned point x and count c are the components of that successful run; the conclusion places no further condition on t. The same fixed next, update and s₀ must meet the premise uniformly over g and its qualifying minimizers before the conclusion applies uniformly over f and its qualifying minimizers. The theorem is conditional on that solver guarantee and does not assert that such a solver exists for an arbitrary φ. Only explicit calls through the execution oracle are counted; arbitrary computation inside the supplied functions is uncharged.
objects: A space E, state type S, β,u,R,ε; an arbitrary natural-valued budget function φ; fixed next, update and s₀; δ,N and corrected defined as in the statement; objectives g and f with qualifying minimizers w and z; successful-run witnesses t,x,c.
domains: E is a proper complete real inner-product space; S is any type; β∈ℝ≥0; u,w,z,x∈E; R,ε∈ℝ>0; φ:ℝ→ℕ; δ∈ℝ≥0 with real value ε/R²; N,c∈ℕ; t,s₀∈S. next:S→E⊕E; update:S→E→(ℝ×E)→S. Objectives have domain E and codomain ℝ.
quantifiers: Universally quantify E,S and space instances, then β,u,R,ε and the positivity and scale hypotheses, then φ,next,update,s₀. Define δ,N. Assume ∀g satisfying the stated differential, strong convexity and smoothness hypotheses, ∀ qualifying minimizers w, ∃t,x,c giving successful ε/2 accuracy. Define corrected. Conclude ∀f satisfying the stated differential, convexity and smoothness hypotheses, ∀ qualifying minimizers z, ∃t,x,c giving the successful ε accuracy and both count bounds. There is no existential solver choice nested under the objective quantifiers.
assumptions: R>0; ε>0; ε≤βR²; all specified space structure; and the uniform strong-convexity solver premise for the fixed machinery. For a concluded f,z: everywhere differentiability, global convexity, β-Lipschitz gradient, global optimality of z and ‖z−u‖≤R. No regularity, monotonicity or positivity of φ beyond φ:ℝ→ℕ is assumed.
conclusion: An exact execution equality to ((t,some x),c), objective error f(x)−f(z)≤ε, and simultaneously c≤⌈φ(2βR²/ε) log 2⌉₊ and c≤φ(2βR²/ε). Fuel N equals the first displayed bound because δ=ε/R². The corrected update simulates adding a centered quadratic to objective values and its gradient term to gradient answers.
scopes: All statements about objectives and their gradients are global on E. The R restriction applies to the qualifying minimizers relative to u; it does not impose a domain or iterate constraint. Both executions start at the same s₀ and use the same next and N. The conclusion replaces only update by corrected and feeds the f value-gradient oracle. Witnesses may depend on the quantified objective and chosen qualifying minimizer. Count concerns explicit oracle invocations only.
constant_dependencies: δ=ε/R² and N=⌈φ(2β/δ) log(δR²/(ε/2))⌉₊=⌈φ(2βR²/ε) log 2⌉₊. The conclusion bound also includes φ(2βR²/ε) without a ceiling/log factor. The guarantee is uniform over objectives for fixed β,u,R,ε,φ,next,update,s₀. No monotonicity of φ is needed for the substitution of equal arguments.
